newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ticket agency to take on airline giants.
newsitem.headline: Japan ticket agency to take on airline giants.

text.p: Japanese airlines face the prospect of growing competition in the domestic market after a Tokyo discount ticket agency said on Monday that it plans to launch internal flights in the next few years.
The company, H.I.S. Co Ltd, would be the first new challenger in the Japanese domestic market -- where flights are expensive by international standards -- in more than four decades.

H.I.S. Co Ltd said that it plans to start regular domestic flights in two to three years' time in competition with the three major airline companies which now dominate the Japanese market. These are Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL), All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA) and Japan Air System Co Ltd.

An H.I.S. spokesman said the firm, which currently sells discounted airline tickets, plans to set up a new company in Tokyo next month to realise its aim of becoming a domestic flight operator. The firm will be capitalised at between 100 million yen ($892,000) and 200 million yen ($1.78 million) and H.I.S. will take a stake of between 30 and 70 percent in it, the spokesman said. H.I.S. said it aimed to apply for a government licence early next year to operate the domestic flights.
After that, it plans to become an airline operator with additional capital of several billion yen. This would make it the first new company to offer domestic, nationwide flights in 43 years.

The company plans to rent three aircraft from leasing companies with a capacity of about 300 passengers each, the spokesman said. Junichi Ogawara of Japan Associated Finance Co Ltd, Japan's largest venture capital firm, is expected to take the helm of the new company, he said.
Media reports said that H.I.S. plans to hire foreign pilots and crew at lower salaries than those paid to Japanese crew.
H.I.S. is currently negotiating with ANA, Japan's second largest airline, about some form of cooperation in the new venture, the spokesman said.
Japan's big airlines are already under pressure from high overheads in Japan and rising oil prices.
A return flight on ANA between Tokyo and Sapporo in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost main island, costs 48,500 yen ($433) for an 895 km (560 mile) journey. $1=111 yen
